reasoning: The package contains standard AUR packaging files for a KDE Plasma binary application. The PKGBUILD fetches a pinned source tarball from GitHub, and the install/hook scripts perform routine cache refreshes. The disagreement was solely caused by an API error in the first model when reviewing non-executable files (.SRCINFO, LICENSE), not by any security concerns.
disagreement_analysis: The first model (qwen) encountered HTTP 400 errors when auditing .SRCINFO and LICENSE, resulting in an overall 'inconclusive' verdict despite marking the executable files as safe. The second model (deepseek) successfully audited all files and correctly concluded the package is safe.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to audit .SRCINFO and LICENSE due to LLM API HTTP 400 errors.
learnings: The audit tool should differentiate between critical execution files (PKGBUILD, .install, hooks) and non-executable metadata files (LICENSE, .SRCINFO) when aggregating verdicts. An API failure on a LICENSE file should not force an overall 'inconclusive' verdict if all executable vectors are verified safe.
Implement retry logic or fallback mechanisms for transient LLM API errors to prevent partial audit failures from skewing the final package verdict.
